studio.global.sub: The settings of the pedal's GLOBAL screen: they sound at once, and the pedal stores them two seconds after the last change.
studio.global.about_eq: The equalizer after the chain, in every preset.
studio.global.about_io: The input's type and level, the AUX input and which outputs the cab blocks play on.
studio.global.about_tuner: The tuner's reference, the sound while tuning and the display type.
studio.global.about_usb: The USB audio channels, the recording and return levels and what goes to each recorded channel.
studio.global.about_jack: What is plugged into the EXP 2 jack and the function of each external footswitch.
studio.global.about_midi: Where the pedal receives MIDI from, on which channels, and the tempo clock.
studio.global.about_presets: What applies to every preset: global tempo, spillover, knobs in scene and the cab engine.
studio.global.about_screen: The display's brightness and the touch mark.
studio.global.about_exp: The calibrated range of each expression pedal.
studio.global.about_system: The temperature of the pedal's processor, as in GLOBAL › SYSTEM.
studio.global.no_temp: The pedal's waveod ({version}) does not measure the temperature yet: write a newer firmware.
studio.global.span_title: Lowest to highest since the pedal was turned on
studio.global.temp_hint: Highest and lowest since the pedal was turned on. The temperature comes from the processor's own sensor (i.MX RT1062), factory calibrated; it is the chip's, hotter than the enclosure's.
studio.global.cabs_hint: where the Cab / IR blocks play
studio.global.usb_mode_hint: the computer sees the pedal again with the other configuration
studio.global.tempo_hint: on, the effects follow this tempo instead of each preset's
studio.global.spill_hint: delays and reverbs ringing over the next preset
studio.global.scene_knobs_hint: Auto: a knob turned while scenes are in use goes into them
studio.global.cab_engine_hint: the preset reloads on the other engine
studio.global.exp_note: Calibrate on the pedal: GLOBAL › EXP PEDALS › CALIBRATE.
studio.eq.title: Global EQ
studio.eq.sub: after the chain, in every preset
studio.eq.flat_title: Every gain at 0 dB, the cuts off, the level at 50
studio.pedal.store: {kb} KB in use · {free} of {sectors} sectors free. waveod's presets, rhythms and controls live in an area no firmware update erases.
studio.pedal.fw_text: Writes a waveod .bin (or the original firmware, to go back) over USB, like the original editor: the pedal restarts in update mode and receives the firmware. The waveod presets, the NAM captures and the user IRs are kept; the original presets go back to the file's. Make a backup first.
studio.pedal.lat_text: The pedal measures how long the sound takes from the input to the output. With a cable from the chosen output to the input, the test plays a click on that output (turn off the amplifier and the headphones). Without a cable, it measures how much the active preset adds. The same test is in GLOBAL › LATENCY on the pedal.
studio.pedal.preset_adds: what the active preset adds to the pedal's latency
studio.pedal.why_preset: the preset did not let the signal through (gate? volume?)
studio.pedal.why_nothing: nothing came back: check the cable and the route
studio.pedal.why_clip: the input clipped already at -30 dBFS: use the LINE input type (GLOBAL)
studio.pedal.no_measure: No measurement. The buffers alone make 128 samples (2.90 ms) at 44.1 kHz.
studio.pedal.dump_text: Reads the pedal's flash memory into a file, without writing anything to it. The whole copy keeps everything (presets, rhythms, captures, IRs, effects) and works as a full backup; over USB it takes a few minutes.
studio.pedal.dump_open_title: The summary of an 8 MB copy made before
studio.pedal.map_aria: Flash map: how much each area uses
studio.pedal.cable_l: a cable from output L to the input (INPUT)
studio.pedal.cable_r: a cable from output R to the input (INPUT)
studio.pedal.cable_send: a cable from FX SEND to FX RETURN
studio.pedal.fw_done_text: {file} ({version}) written in {time}. The pedal restarts with it and the Studio connects by itself when it is back. Log: {log}
studio.pedal.fw_failed_text: {error}. The pedal should be in update mode (the bootloader is never rewritten): you can try again. If it does not answer, turn it on holding the update mode's footswitch combination.
studio.pedal.measure_text: Connect {cable}. The test plays a click on that output: turn off the amplifier and the headphones first.
studio.fw.title: Update the pedal's firmware
studio.fw.note_boot: The pedal restarts in update mode (bootloader) and receives the four sections over USB, as in the original editor. The bootloader is never rewritten: a write that fails can be repeated.
studio.fw.note_keep: The waveod presets, rhythms and controls, the NAM captures (Clone) and the user IRs are outside the written sections and are kept. The Bank section is rewritten: the list's original presets go back to the file's. Make a backup first (Presets › Backup): it keeps both kinds.
studio.fw.note_power: Do not turn the pedal off or unplug the cable during the write.
studio.fw.agree: I understand: the pedal has no sound during the write, which takes a few minutes.
studio.perf.sub: Cycles of the pedal's processor per block of 64 samples (1.451 ms at 44.1 kHz). Measured on the pedal itself.
studio.perf.unsupported: The pedal's firmware (protocol {protocol}) does not measure cycles: write a waveod with protocol 11 or newer.
studio.perf.emu_text: the cycles here are worth nothing (the emulator's counter moves a fixed step per reading); the CRC counts, and matches the pedal's when the code computes the same.
studio.perf.spark_aria: Block use over the last readings
studio.perf.between: Between the slots (the chain without the effects)
studio.perf.profile_note_one: {n} block since the previous reading · core at {mhz} MHz · each slot measured inside the audio interrupt, with the real cache and signal.
studio.perf.profile_note_other: {n} blocks since the previous reading · core at {mhz} MHz · each slot measured inside the audio interrupt, with the real cache and signal.
studio.perf.bench_text: The pedal loads the effect on its own and plays a test signal through it: the audio is muted for a few seconds and the preset comes back as it was. A file goes only to the RAM (nothing is written) and is read from the disk again at every measurement; a block's .c source is built by the SDK first (src/sdk/wvfx.h). With Watch, each time the file is saved it is measured again: edit, save, compare.
studio.perf.watch_title: Measures again each time the file is saved
studio.perf.watch_title_src: Measures again each time the file (or a .c / .h in the same folder) is saved
studio.perf.cold_title: Clears the data cache before each block: the worst case (delay lines and tables come from the SDRAM)
studio.perf.bypass_title: Measures the cost of the slot when off
studio.perf.again_file: Measure again (the file is read again)
studio.perf.foot: Δ is the median against the reference; same CRC = the same output, bit for bit (the test signal is always the same).
studio.perf.crc_changed: {name}: the CRC changed ({from} → {to}): the output is not the same as the reference's
